feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism is real. The built `.output/public/assets/styles-DjfYz07w.css` has 670 blocks of `@supports (color:color-mix(in lab,red,red))`: 576 in utilities, 82 top-level hand CSS, 9 in components. They come from Tailwind's `Polyfills.ColorMix` pass (`node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/lib.js`, enum `St` ColorMix=2, guarded by `r&2`).

My AST simulation (`verdicts/css-C5/sim.mjs`) reproduces the byte claim: -74 314 B raw, -5 305 B gzip-6, -3 501 B br-11.

No gate is violated:
- publicCss (`check-bundle-size.ts:2022`, `:2456-2461`) only gets smaller.
- `noHasSelectors.test.ts` and `searchOverflowCascade.test.ts:21` read the source `src/styles.css`, which a build-time strip does not change.
- There is no SSR, hydration or chunk-graph effect.

But the change is under-specified and its "already wrong" premise is partly false:
1. There is no config knob. `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3 never passes `polyfills` to `compile` (0 occurrences in `dist/index.mjs`). Its `generate:build` transform is `enforce:"pre"`, and `vite.config.ts:101` has no CSS post-step. So it needs a bun patch, a lightningcss visitor (the Lovable config sets `css.transformer: "lightningcss"`, `@lovable.dev/vite-tanstack-config/dist/index.js:1600`) or a custom post-transform plugin. Doing it in `generateBundle` would leave the content hash stale.
2. Of the 622 paired fallbacks, 183 are correct pre-resolved hex+alpha values, e.g. `.border-amber-300\/50{border-color:#ffd23680}`. C5 makes them IACVT (`unset`) on browsers without color-mix. Only 350 opaque `var()` fallbacks and 87 opaque box-shadows are "wrong anyway".
3. 48 blocks set `--tw-ring-color`. Without color-mix, the focus-visible ring box-shadow becomes invalid and disappears on Safari 15.4-16.1 and Firefox below 113. That is an a11y regression; today the ring is opaque but visible.
4. The JS floor is below color-mix. Vite 7.3.6 with no `build.target` defaults to safari16 / chrome107 / firefox104 (the comment at `src/lib/observability/redact.ts:55` still says Safari 14). This is mitigated because the code already uses unguarded color-mix in 309 places in TS/TSX and 49 times in production inline styles, and the tokens are oklch (`styles.css:303-320`).
5. 53 inner rules have no adjacent same-selector fallback because lightningcss merged them, so a regex strip would mis-pair them.

A hybrid is better: keep the literal fallback and drop color-mix where the fallback is resolved; drop the fallback where it is `var()`. It gives -83 119 raw / -5 595 gzip / -3 531 br and has no palette regression.
blocking_issues: Needs an explicit browser-floor decision (Safari >=16.2, Firefox >=113, Chrome >=111). The Vite 7 default JS target (safari16/chrome107/firefox104) still boots browsers that lack color-mix.

There is no Tailwind/Vite option: @tailwindcss/vite does not expose `polyfills`. It needs a bun patch, a lightningcss visitor or a post-transform plugin with correct hashing, plus a test on the built sheet. Effort S is optimistic.
183 of 622 fallbacks are correct hex+alpha values (Tailwind-resolved palette colours). C5 as written regresses them. Use the hybrid instead: keep the literal and drop the color-mix branch.
48 --tw-ring-color blocks would make focus-visible rings vanish on non-color-mix browsers (a11y). Either exclude them or accept that under the floor decision.
53 @supports rules have no adjacent same-selector fallback (merged by lightningcss), so the strip must be an AST pass, not a regex.
effect_reasoning:
The sheet is VeryHigh and render-blocking, so it is on the critical path, and the bytes are real.

Transfer delta:
- PSI: about -5.3 KB. PSI transfer of 78 624 B is about the gzip-6 size, so production serves gzip.
- Fixture: about -3.5 to -4 KB br.

Elasticity:
- lighthouse-analyst's deterministic what-if: CSS -70 % (-49 KB) gives FCP 0 ms (FCP is JS-bound because the modulepreloaded chunks sit in the FCP graph) and LCP -225 ms, i.e. 4.6 ms/KB on LCP only.
- css.md A/B: 4-6 ms/KB.

Mobile:
- LCP: 5.3 KB x 4.6 ms/KB = about -24 ms. FCP: 0 to -25 ms.
- Score at the PSI operating point (LCP -1 s is worth +2.3 pts, FCP -1 s is worth +3.5 pts): 0.024 x 2.3 + up to 0.025 x 3.5 = about +0.06 to +0.15 pt.
- At the target operating point (LCP about 2.8 s, about 6.7 pts/s; FCP about 2 s, about 3.3 pts/s): about +0.25 pt at most.

Desktop: about 1 ms/KB x 5 KB = 5 ms, so 0 pts.

TBT: 0. The 74 KB less CSS parse happens before FCP, and pre-FCP CPU is irrelevant (shrinking it to 5 % moves FCP 55 ms). The 670 duplicate class rules do not measurably change post-hydration recalc.

The proposed acceptance test ("FCP/LCP medians move about 5 ms per KB br") cannot be measured. The expected delta is about 20 ms, but `measure-ab.sh` noise at n=3 on this shared host is about ±100 ms, so I deliberately ran no Lighthouse what-if. The value of the change is gate headroom (publicCss 83 KB, the proposed <=45 KB render-blocking target in C11), not score. Nothing cheaper gives the same bytes; it is already cheap.
corrected_estimate:
Bytes as specified: -74 KB raw / -5.3 KB gzip-6 / -3.5 KB br-11 (claimed -69 KB / -5.0 KB). The hybrid variant gives -83 KB raw / -5.6 KB gzip / -3.5 KB br with no palette regression. At stage 3 it is about -3.7 KB gzip.

Mobile:
- LCP -15 to -25 ms (5.3 KB x 4.6 ms/KB)
- FCP 0 to -25 ms
- about +0.1 pt now, at most +0.25 pt at the 85-target operating point

Desktop: FCP/LCP about -5 ms, 0 pts. TBT: 0 on both form factors.

Do not count it toward the 85/95 path. Ship only as budget headroom for C11, in the hybrid form, after the floor decision. Verify it statically (built-sheet bytes in check:bundle), not with A/B.
better_alternative:
Hybrid strip:
- For fallbacks Tailwind already resolved to a literal (183 palette colours such as #ffd23680), keep the literal and drop the @supports color-mix branch.
- For `var()` fallbacks (350 colours + 87 box-shadows), keep color-mix and drop the fallback.
- Optionally leave the 48 --tw-ring-color blocks untouched to keep focus rings on old Safari (about 0.3 KB gzip).

Measured: -83 119 B raw / -5 595 B gzip-6 / -3 531 B br-11. Implement it as a lightningcss visitor or a bun patch of @tailwindcss/vite passing `polyfills: Polyfills.AtProperty`, so the asset hash stays correct.
